messages:
jordan: FYI noticed a user-reported double-charge in the console tied to a long streaming request that triggered a tool call mid-stream. looks like router swapped backends and the toolcall got retried and charged twice. anyone seen this pattern?

sam: can you paste the logs or the session id?

jordan: pasted below. session=svc-xt9, request_id=0x7f2a. timeline: client stream -> streaming chunk -> TOOL_CALL -> reconnect to new router -> resume -> trailing truncation + duplicate TOOL_CALL event.

jordan: ```
[2026-02-18T14:02:01Z] session svc-xt9 seq=1 chunk=...
[2026-02-18T14:02:05Z] TOOL_CALL id=tc-88 seq=42 routed->node-a
[2026-02-18T14:02:06Z] node-a lost lease, handoff to node-b
[2026-02-18T14:02:07Z] resume token rt=abc123 seq=43 routed->node-b
[2026-02-18T14:02:07Z] TOOL_CALL id=tc-88 replay seq=42 routed->node-b
[2026-02-18T14:02:07Z] stream truncated suffix_len=12
```

priya: console metrics show a small spike in provisional charges around that timeframe. customers see two toolcall token entries in the ledger (one provisional, one confirmed).

angela: this smells like session-affinity vs. idempotency mismatch. our router handoff keeps session on last-node heuristics but toolcalls are only deduped by toolcall-id when originating node attaches a claim. if handoff doesn't carry claim metadata, node-b treats it as fresh.

matt: agreed. two quick mitigations: 1) include origin-session-id+toolcall-id in billing dedupe key, 2) attach a short-lived "call-claim" token for toolcalls that gets forwarded during handoff.

sam: both sound good. is there any reason we can't make dedupe key include resume-token+toolcall-id? would that break any current assumptions?

angela: resume-token not always present (short streams). also resume-token changes on partial truncation. safer to use session_id + client_seq + toolcall_id. session_id persists across handoffs.

jordan: can we avoid altering billing ledger schema? ops expects minimal changes. if we do dedupe at ingestion layer (pre-ledger) we can keep ledger unchanged and drop duplicates before commit.

matt: yes, we can add an ingestion filter that dedups based on composite key (session_id|toolcall_id|seq). that filter needs to be idempotent and tolerant to clock skew.

priya: console UX question: customers currently see two entries (one provisional flagged). if we dedupe pre-ledger, do we reconcile existing double-charges or leave them as manual refunds?

angela: we should run a backfill to mark duplicates and issue credits for confirmed double-charges. small opt-in job first.

sam: for short-term alerting — add a dashboard panel that shows toolcall duplicate rate per router version / canary bucket. that should help correlate to rollout toggles.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary router changes to sticky-affinity v2 at 2026-02-19T03:00Z (sha=deadbeef).

jordan: ok action items I can take: 1) produce repro harness with forced handoff + toolcall replay, 2) add logs to include session_id in toolcall telemetry, 3) open billing-ingest PR to dedupe using (session|toolcall|seq). assigning owners?

matt: I'll take billing-ingest PR.

angela: I'll own the canary observation and add the dashboard tile.

priya: I'll scope the backfill credits job and customer comms if needed.

sam: I'll review the repro harness and help with the alert thresholds.

jordan: thanks — will post the repro link and sample traces in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:

matt: one more ask — make sure the ingestion dedupe exposes a metric for "dropped duplicate charges" so finance can audit.

jordan: will do.

priya: small note — if toolcall contains side-effecting calls we should ensure retries are safe. dedupe for billing doesn't equal dedupe for external side-effects. add a flag to only dedupe billing records, not suppress actual tool invocation retries for now.

angela: good point. separate the control-plane dedupe for accounting from the runtime invocation semantics.

jordan: noted. will keep that separation in the repro and the PR.

sam: cool. if anyone spots a customer impacted, ping @oncall to temp pause canary.

ops-bot: @oncall pager: no current incidents.

jordan: thread closed for now, will re-open with repro + PR link.
